def-quasi-bialgebra-and-quasi-hopf-algeb:
## Definition

Fix a field $k$ and use algebraic tensor products over $k$ as in [[def-hh-scalar-and-tensor-conventions]]. A **quasi-bialgebra** is an associative unital $k$-algebra $H$ (in the sense of [[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) with unital algebra maps $\Delta:H\to H\otimes H$ and $\varepsilon:H\to k$, and an invertible element $\Phi\in H^{\otimes 3}$, satisfying the counit identities $(\varepsilon\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta=\mathrm{id}=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta$, the quasi-coassociativity identity
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Delta(h)=\Phi\,(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(h)\,\Phi^{-1}\qquad(h\in H),$$
the pentagon identity
$$(1\otimes\Phi)(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})(\Phi)(\Phi\otimes1)=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)(\Phi)(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}\otimes\mathrm{id})(\Phi),$$
and the normalization $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\varepsilon\otimes\mathrm{id})(\Phi)=1\otimes1$. Here $\Phi$ is the **reassociator**. With this convention, $\Phi$ acts from the left-parenthesized tensor product to the right-parenthesized one. When $\Phi=1$, these conditions give the ordinary bialgebra axioms of [[def-hh-bialgebra-and-bialgebra-map]].

A **quasi-antipode** for a quasi-bialgebra is a triple $(S,\alpha,\beta)$ where $S:H\to H$ is a unital algebra antihomomorphism and $\alpha,\beta\in H$ satisfy
$$\sum S(h_{(1)})\alpha h_{(2)}=\varepsilon(h)\alpha,\qquad \sum h_{(1)}\beta S(h_{(2)})=\varepsilon(h)\beta,$$
$$\sum X^1\beta S(X^2)\alpha X^3=1,\qquad \sum S(x^1)\alpha x^2\beta S(x^3)=1,$$
where $\Delta(h)=\sum h_{(1)}\otimes h_{(2)}$, $\Phi=\sum X^1\otimes X^2\otimes X^3$, and $\Phi^{-1}=\sum x^1\otimes x^2\otimes x^3$. A **quasi-Hopf algebra** is a quasi-bialgebra with a quasi-antipode whose map $S$ is bijective. A quasi-bialgebra need not have a quasi-antipode, and a quasi-antipode is additional data rather than part of the quasi-bialgebra structure.
def-weak-bialgebra-and-weak-hopf-algebra:
## Definition

Fix a field $k$, an associative unital $k$-algebra $H$ (as in [[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]), and a coassociative counital coalgebra structure $(\Delta,\varepsilon)$ as in [[def-hh-coalgebra-and-coalgebra-map]]. Write $\Delta(h)=\sum h_{(1)}\otimes h_{(2)}$ and suppress the finite Sweedler sums. A **weak bialgebra** is these structures with multiplicative coproduct $\Delta(ab)=\Delta(a)\Delta(b)$, not necessarily a unital algebra map, and with the following weak unit and weak counit identities:
$$ (\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(1)=(\Delta(1)\otimes1)(1\otimes\Delta(1))=(1\otimes\Delta(1))(\Delta(1)\otimes1), $$
$$ \varepsilon(abc)=\sum\varepsilon(ab_{(1)})\varepsilon(b_{(2)}c)=\sum\varepsilon(ab_{(2)})\varepsilon(b_{(1)}c)\qquad(a,b,c\in H). $$
In general $\Delta(1)\ne1\otimes1$ and $\varepsilon$ is not multiplicative.

For $\Delta(1)=\sum1_{(1)}\otimes1_{(2)}$, define the **target** and **source counital maps**
$$ \varepsilon_t(h)=\sum\varepsilon(1_{(1)}h)1_{(2)},\qquad \varepsilon_s(h)=\sum1_{(1)}\varepsilon(h1_{(2)}). $$
Write $H_t=\varepsilon_t(H)$ and $H_s=\varepsilon_s(H)$. The source-and-target-bases lemma below proves these ranges are commuting unital subalgebras. We also use the variant
$$ \varepsilon_s'(h)=\sum1_{(1)}\varepsilon(1_{(2)}h). $$
The same lemma proves that its restriction to $H_t$ is the inverse anti-isomorphism to $\varepsilon_t|_{H_s}$.

A **weak Hopf algebra** is a weak bialgebra with a linear map $S:H\to H$ satisfying
$$ \sum h_{(1)}S(h_{(2)})=\varepsilon_t(h),\qquad \sum S(h_{(1)})h_{(2)}=\varepsilon_s(h),\qquad \sum S(h_{(1)})h_{(2)}S(h_{(3)})=S(h). $$
No bijectivity of $S$ is imposed in this definition. The module tensor product below uses the source-target maps and does not require an antipode.
thm-quasi-bialgebra-modules-form-a-monoi:
## Statement

Let $(H,\Delta,\varepsilon,\Phi)$ be a quasi-bialgebra over a field $k$ in the convention of [[def-quasi-bialgebra-and-quasi-hopf-algebra]]. The category $H\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ of unital left $H$-modules, with $H$-linear maps, is monoidal. Its tensor product has underlying vector space $V\otimes_k W$ and action
$$h\cdot(v\otimes w)=\sum h_{(1)}v\otimes h_{(2)}w.$$
Its unit object is $k_\varepsilon=k$ with $h\cdot c=\varepsilon(h)c$. The associator from $(U\otimes V)\otimes W$ to $U\otimes(V\otimes W)$ is the canonical vector-space rebracketing followed by the action of $\Phi$:
$$a_{U,V,W}((u\otimes v)\otimes w)=\sum \Phi^1u\otimes(\Phi^2v\otimes\Phi^3w),\qquad \Phi=\sum\Phi^1\otimes\Phi^2\otimes\Phi^3.$$
The left and right unit constraints are the canonical vector-space maps. No quasi-antipode is needed for this monoidal structure.
lem-weak-bialgebra-source-and-target-bas:
## Statement

Let $H$ be a weak bialgebra over a field $k$, with counital maps $\varepsilon_t,\varepsilon_s$ and images $H_t,H_s$ as in [[def-weak-bialgebra-and-weak-hopf-algebra]]. Then $\varepsilon_t$ and $\varepsilon_s$ are idempotent projections, $H_t$ and $H_s$ are unital subalgebras that commute elementwise, and $\varepsilon_t|_{H_s}:H_s\to H_t$ is an algebra anti-isomorphism whose inverse is $\varepsilon_s'|_{H_t}$. For $g,h\in H$ and $x,z\in H_t$,
$$\varepsilon_t(gh)=\varepsilon_t(g\varepsilon_t(h)),\qquad \varepsilon_t(xh)=x\varepsilon_t(h),\qquad \varepsilon_t(\varepsilon_s'(x)z)=zx.$$
The element
$$e=(\varepsilon_t\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(1)=\sum e^1\otimes e^2\in H_t\otimes H_t$$
is a separability idempotent for $H_t$, meaning that its product is $1$ and it centralizes $H_t$; for every $x\in H_t$ it also satisfies
$$\sum\varepsilon(xe^1)e^2=x,\qquad \sum e^1\varepsilon(e^2x)=x,\qquad \sum e^1e^2=1,\qquad \sum xe^1\otimes e^2=\sum e^1\otimes e^2x.$$
Moreover, $\Delta(1)=\sum\varepsilon_s'(e^1)\otimes e^2$. For $h\in H$ and $x\in H_t$ the identities
$$\sum\varepsilon_t(h_{(1)}x)h_{(2)}=hx,\qquad \sum\varepsilon_s'(\varepsilon_t(h_{(2)}x))h_{(1)}=h\varepsilon_s'(x)$$
hold. These are the counital-base identities used for the relative tensor product and its unit maps.
prop-weak-bialgebra-module-tensor-produc:
## Statement

Let $H$ be a weak bialgebra over a field $k$, and let $V,W$ be unital left $H$-modules. Give $V$ the right $H_t$-action $v\triangleleft x=\varepsilon_s'(x)v$ and give $W$ its left $H_t$-action by restriction. The diagonal action of $H$ descends to the balanced tensor product $V\otimes_{H_t}W$. The map
$$[v\otimes w]\longmapsto\Delta(1)\cdot(v\otimes w)=\sum1_{(1)}v\otimes1_{(2)}w$$
is a natural isomorphism
$$V\otimes_{H_t}W\ \cong\ \Delta(1)(V\otimes_kW).$$
With this action, the category of unital left $H$-modules is monoidal: its associator is the restriction of the vector-space rebracketing map, and its unit is $H_t$ with action $h\cdot x=\varepsilon_t(hx)$. This proposition applies in particular to a weak Hopf algebra; its antipode is not used.
ex-two-object-discrete-groupoid-is-a-wea:
## Statement

Let $H=\mathbb C e_0\oplus\mathbb C e_1$ with $e_i e_j=\delta_{ij}e_i$, unit $1=e_0+e_1$, coproduct $\Delta(e_i)=e_i\otimes e_i$, counit $\varepsilon(e_i)=1$, and antipode $S(e_i)=e_i$. Then $H$ is a weak Hopf algebra with $H_t=H_s=H$ and
$$\Delta(1)=e_0\otimes e_0+e_1\otimes e_1\ne1\otimes1.$$
For any left $H$-modules $V,W$, give $V$ the right $H_t$-action $v\triangleleft x=\varepsilon_s'(x)v$ and let $H_t$ act on $W$ by restriction. Here $V\otimes_{H_t}W$ is the quotient of $V\otimes_kW$ by the span of $(v\triangleleft x)\otimes w-v\otimes xw$. The induced diagonal action is $e_i\cdot[v\otimes w]=[e_iv\otimes e_iw]$, and this relative tensor product is naturally isomorphic as a left $H$-module to
$$e_0V\otimes e_0W\ \oplus\ e_1V\otimes e_1W=\Delta(1)(V\otimes W).$$
The counit is not multiplicative, so this weak Hopf algebra is not an ordinary bialgebra.
ex-quasi-hopf-algebra-from-the-nontrivia:
## Statement

Let $G=C_2=\{0,1\}$ with addition modulo $2$, let $H=k^G$ over $k=\mathbb C$, and set
$$\Delta(p_g)=\sum_{a+b=g}p_a\otimes p_b,\qquad \varepsilon(p_g)=\begin{cases}1&g=0,\\0&g=1,\end{cases}$$
for the delta-function basis $(p_0,p_1)$. Define $\omega(a,b,c)=(-1)^{abc}$ for $a,b,c\in\{0,1\}$ and
$$\Phi=\sum_{a,b,c\in C_2}\omega(a,b,c)p_a\otimes p_b\otimes p_c.$$
$$\alpha=p_0-p_1,\qquad \beta=p_0+p_1,\qquad S(p_g)=p_g.$$
These data define a quasi-Hopf algebra. Its associator acts by $-1$ on the triple tensor product of three copies of the degree-$1$ simple module. This example asserts $\Phi\ne1$ as an element of $H^{\otimes3}$; it does not assert that the quasi-Hopf algebra is not twist-equivalent to a Hopf algebra.
